TX.name: Telehealth Informed Consent - Texas
TX.html:
Identity Aesthetics PLLC — Telehealth Informed Consent: Texas

This consent applies to telehealth care you receive from Identity Aesthetics while you are physically located in the State of Texas. Please read it carefully. You may ask questions before you sign.

1. What telehealth is. Telehealth means your provider evaluates, diagnoses and treats you using real-time, two-way audio and video instead of an in-person visit. Your provider may also review photos, forms, lab results and secure messages you send.

2. Your provider and their license. Your telehealth care in Texas is provided by Dallas Alvey, MD; Sarah Walker, APRN; or Javier Gonzalez, MD, each licensed in Texas. You may ask your provider to confirm their name, credentials and license at any time, and you can verify any license with the Texas Medical Board.

3. Where you must be. You confirm that you are physically located in Texas at the time of every telehealth visit, and you will tell us if you are somewhere else. If you are outside Texas or another state where we are licensed, we cannot treat you that day. You must be 18 or older.

4. Services available in Texas. Through telehealth in Texas we offer medical weight loss (including GLP-1 medicines), compounded peptide therapy, hormone and wellness consultations, and Vyleesi. Aesthetic injections, laser treatments and other procedures are not performed by telehealth. Controlled substances are prescribed only by a provider who holds a DEA registration for Texas, only when clinically appropriate, and only as federal and Texas telemedicine rules allow.

5. Identity and the first visit. You agree to upload a valid photo ID and to verify your identity at the start of each visit. Your first visit is a real-time video visit before any prescription is written.

6. Benefits. Telehealth can give you faster access to care, less travel and care from home.

7. Risks and limits. Telehealth has risks, including: (a) your provider cannot do a hands-on physical exam, so some conditions may be missed or need an in-person visit, labs or testing; (b) technology can fail, causing delays or a lost connection; (c) despite reasonable security, electronic information could be intercepted or accessed without permission; and (d) your provider may decide telehealth is not appropriate for you and refer you to in-person care. A prescription is never guaranteed.

8. Your rights. You may decline telehealth or withdraw this consent at any time, without losing access to care you are otherwise entitled to. You may ask for in-person care instead; in-person visits are available at our Texas offices. You may request a copy of your medical records. Visits are not recorded without your separate permission.

9. Privacy. Your visit uses OptiMantra, a secure electronic health record and telehealth platform covered by a HIPAA business associate agreement. Join from a private place. Others present during your visit must be identified to your provider. Your information is protected as described in our Notice of Privacy Practices.

10. Prescriptions and pharmacy. If your provider prescribes a medicine, it is sent to Total Apothecary Pharmacy (Stafford, Texas) or another licensed pharmacy you choose. Compounded medicines are not FDA-approved and are prescribed only when your provider documents a medical reason. The pharmacy bills you for the medicine separately.

11. Emergencies. Telehealth is not for emergencies. If you have a medical emergency, call 911 or go to the nearest emergency room. Tell your provider your location and a phone number at the start of each visit so we can reach you or send help if the connection drops.

12. Follow-up and care coordination. Your provider will tell you how to get follow-up care. With your permission, we may share your visit records with your primary care provider.

13. Fees. The $100 initial fee is paid when you book and is non-refundable, including if you cancel, miss your visit, or your provider decides not to prescribe. Telehealth care is self-pay; we do not bill insurance.

14. Complaints. You may contact Identity Aesthetics at 713-268-6963 or info@713botoxme.com with any concern. You may also file a complaint with the Texas Medical Board, www.tmb.state.tx.us, 1-800-201-9353.

Texas notice concerning complaints. Complaints about physicians, as well as other licensees and registrants of the Texas Medical Board, may be reported for investigation to the Texas Medical Board at www.tmb.state.tx.us or 1-800-201-9353. Complaints about advanced practice registered nurses may be reported to the Texas Board of Nursing at www.bon.texas.gov.

Acknowledgment. By signing, I confirm that I have read and understand this consent, that I had the chance to ask questions, that I am 18 or older, that I am physically located in Texas, and that I voluntarily consent to receive care through telehealth from Identity Aesthetics.
